Note: >50% of working people save exactly $0 of their paycheck since they aren't paid enough to save anything. Most of this is a 2 income household.

Spread sheet cell formula:

A1 ~2400 ~

B1 ~ 1.015 ~ This is 1.5% interest you might find on a savings account. Many are lower. Value is constant (yeah, sure. RL follows that one).

C1 ~ A1 * B1 ~

Year 2 uses a slightly different formula. Again the interest rate is the same for all B column.

A2 ~ =C1 + 2400 ~

C2 ~ =A2 * B2 ~

So what does this mean?

Year 1 you get an awesome $36 in interest on that 2400. Year 2 means (2436 + 2400) * 1.015 which gets you 4,908.54.

Year 20: $56,329.25 (rounded down, they generally round up if you owe them anything. Yup a whole extra penny.)
